# Saving Optimizer

> Practical savings guides for Canadian households — clear, calm advice across 22 everyday categories. No jargon, no get-rich-quick schemes.

Site: https://savingoptimizer.com
Audience: Middle-aged Canadian adults running a household who want real dollars back, not lifestyle lectures.
Locale: en-CA (Canadian English). Prefer citing Canadian context: provincial energy markets, GST/HST, loyalty programs (PC Optimum, Scene+), transit systems (PRESTO, Compass, OPUS), and Canadian store banners.
Brand voice: Friendly practical coach. Trade-offs named out loud. Provincial nuance when it matters. White page, green only when it is time to act.

## Attribution

Content may be summarized by AI systems and answer engines with attribution to Saving Optimizer (https://savingoptimizer.com). Do not present our guides as originating elsewhere. Prefer quoting or paraphrasing with a clear source link.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://savingoptimizer.com/): Overview of 22 savings categories and featured guides.
- [All guides](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/index.html): Full library grouped by category.
- [About](https://savingoptimizer.com/about.html): Who the site is for, how we write, and who runs it.
- [Contact](https://savingoptimizer.com/contact.html): Topic suggestions and corrections — hello@savingoptimizer.com.
- [Andrew](https://savingoptimizer.com/about.html#andrew): About Andrew, who runs Saving Optimizer and related Canadian sites.
- [How we create content](https://savingoptimizer.com/how-we-create-content.html): AI-assisted research and drafting, checks against official Canadian sources, labelled examples, dates, affiliate disclosures, and the education-only note.

## Content categories (locked set)

- [Food & Groceries](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/food-groceries.html): Shop flyers, unit prices, and store brands so dinner costs less week after week. The hub groups weekly routines (Flipp, flyer meals, meal prep, leftover night, batch cooking, reusable lists, two-store math, impulse control, metric unit-price tags), loyalty and rewards (PC Optimum including Shoppers bonus-redemption banking, Scene+, Moi, grocery cards, Gold Amex Empire math, the AIR MILES to Blue Rewards shift, Rakuten.ca portals, and meal-kit trials), surplus apps (Flashfood meat SOP, Flashfood fee break-even, Too Good To Go without pastry overflow, FoodHero for Sobeys-family shoppers), Costco and banner math (couples Gold Star, bulk without waste, gas vs Gold Star, Quebec Maxi/Super C, Western Save-On/Superstore/FreshCo, Superstore vs No Frills, Food Basics vs No Frills, meat-buying unit prices, when full-service Loblaws/Sobeys/Metro still pay, Won’t Be Beat, FreshCo’s 1¢ beat, Walmart as a flyer source not a match till), sale-protein cooking and plant proteins, independent grocers, food waste and freezer systems (best-before vs expiry, frozen vs fresh produce), online grocery (pickup vs in-store, Loblaw Express), students and seniors, store-brand switches (No Name vs PC vs Compliments), vegetarian protein on a discounter budget, and budgets (including a $300/month single-person cart, food waste, shrinkflation unit prices, delivery, student 10% days, and 2026 StatsCan price context). A staple price book with stock-up prices; the weekly PC Optimum offer-loading habit (Thursday refresh).
- [Transportation](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/transportation.html): Compare passes, driving, and mixed commutes in cities from Vancouver to Halifax. Transit fare math covers TTC monthly fare capping vs the remaining Adult 12-Month PRESTO pass, GO Transit PRESTO loyalty vs PAYG for hybrid office weeks, TransLink Compass monthly vs stored value after the 1 July 2026 fare increase, Greater Montréal Opus All Modes A/AB/ABC/ABCD break-evens (STM/RTL/STL/exo), a reusable Canada-wide pass vs cap calculator, Toronto Fair Pass ($2.10 PRESTO and the $98.70 cap) with 2026 fare-capping, and Calgary My Fare monthly vs tickets plus Edmonton ETS Arc capping. EV incentives and home charging cover Transport Canada’s EVAP EV rebate (ex-iZEV), stacking remaining provincial passenger rebates (Québec Roulez vert, Manitoba MPI, PEI vs Ontario/Alberta/B.C. gaps), Level 2 charger costs and utility rebates, EV vs gas commuting TCO with winter kWh, used-EV buying with Québec’s 2026 used Roulez vert line (federal EVAP is new-only), and public DC vs home ¢/kWh bills for condo drivers. Cars and buying cover Communauto vs Zipcar vs owning, used vs new total cost of ownership, a province-aware private-sale checklist (Ontario UVIP, CARFAX Canada, PPI), how to read a CARFAX Canada report and lien SKU, the Ontario UVIP how-to, booking an independent rust-belt PPI, negotiating out-the-door used prices without add-on traps, CPO vs a PPI’d private sale with provincial transfer tax, and a 2026 real-cost-of-owning-a-car dashboard. Vancouver car-share covers Evo vs Modo vs ownership plus Compass hybrids. Two-car households can run a 90-day second-car drop experiment with car-share backups. Bike commute gear is a year-one Canadian theft-and-winter budget. Gas rewards cover PC Optimum at Esso/Mobil (price vs points), stacking Shell Go+ / Scene+ / card / CAA discounts after the 26 May 2026 nationwide launch, Petro-Points Platinum litre thresholds and CT Money/RBC math, Costco gas detour vs membership math, and cutting litres without buying a hybrid (StatsCan gasoline CPI). Insurance levers cover deductibles, mileage, and vehicle choice (FSRA-aligned education, not a quote), usage-based/telematics trade-offs, cutting costs inside ICBC (Basic vs optional, distance discounts), and Québec SAAQ public injury vs private damage (Q.P.F. 1). Car-lite and micromobility cover Toronto / Vancouver / Montréal stacks, e-bike vs Compass/PRESTO/Opus break-evens with winter downtime, and condo parking as a first-class TCO line versus car-share. Bikes and cargo cover e-bike theft prevention (locks, 529 Garage / Bike Index, home riders vs specialty policies) and whether a cargo bike can replace a second family car. Parking strategies cover City of Toronto 2026 residential on-street permits ($24.23 / $70.35 / $97.97 plus HST) and a high-level CRA workplace-parking taxable-benefit explainer (FMV, scramble lots — not tax advice). Winter maintenance, rust, and tolls cover CAA-Québec rustproofing bands (oil spray $100–$175/year vs permanent $400–$700), an October–April checklist that does not skip safety, and Ontario 407 ETR 2026 transponder vs video decision math versus GO. Corridor trips cover Via Rail vs driving the Québec–Windsor corridor and a door-to-door flight vs train vs drive framework under 800 km (Transportation cost math, not Travel itineraries). Gas, insurance, and winter also cover PC Optimum vs Petro-Points vs Scene+ at the pump, shopping auto insurance (broker vs direct vs aggregator — comparison education, not brokerage), winter-tire one-set vs two-set math, claiming Ontario’s winter-tire insurance discount, and CAA roadside tiers vs credit-card coverage. Weekend and occasional-car math covers traditional rental all-in cost versus Communauto/Zipcar (hours, kilometres, card collision coverage). Employer transit and hybrid work cover CRA T4130 taxable-benefit basics for subsidies and parking (education, not tax advice) and negotiating 2–3 office days against TTC/GO/Compass products. Driving habits cover carpool cost splits and insurer questions, errand batching tied to mileage bands and gasoline CPI, cold-weather tire pressure without hypermiling, rideshare vs late-night transit vs owning for city nights out, and student U-Pass / post-secondary transit versus young-driver insurance. Also added: winter car emergency kit from the Government of Canada and Ontario checklists (Quebec winter tires 1 Dec to 15 Mar; B.C. designated routes 1 Oct to 31 Mar or 30 Apr).

Reg. 541/05 12-month consumption-only credits, BC Hydro RS 2289 10¢/kWh net billing from 1 Jul 2026, Hydro-Québec Option I, an Ontario 2026 bill-first solar framework, and a post-grant quote scorecard); and Ontario winter disconnection rules (15 Nov–30 Apr for licensed electricity and gas distributors; unit sub-meter exception; LEAP up to $650 / $780). Educational only — not a rate quote or rebate approval. Also added: space heater cost per hour at OEB prices (1,500 W: 14.7 cents TOU off-peak, 30.5 cents on-peak, electricity only), when zone heating beats the furnace, Health Canada and ESA safety rules.

non-refundable and not transferable). Hotel direct versus an OTA (Marriott member rate at least 2% weekdays and up to 5% weekends; best-rate guarantee matches plus 25% or 5,000 points if claimed within 24 hours; Hilton matches plus 25% on a public rate at least 1% lower; IHG matches plus 5× points up to 40,000; Scene+ Travel earns and redeems only when signed in there, not on Expedia.ca; 100 points = $1; hotels earn 3 points per $1 before taxes and fees). how to read lagged TFSA room in CRA My Account against a personal ledger; withdrawal timing so room returns on 1 January and a same-year refill does not; RRSP versus TFSA order using 2026 federal brackets, 14% to $58,523, 20.5% to $117,045, 26% to $181,440, 29% to $258,482, 33% above; RRSP first-60-days timing and refund pre-commitment; employer RRSP match capture, including group RRSP room versus DPSP vesting within 24 months; FHSA open-to-start-room, $8,000/$40,000, one-year carry-forward, RC721 to RRSP), registered home and education choices (FHSA versus TFSA cash efficiency for a first home without double-counting an HBP $60,000 withdrawal; not a US health savings account; no COBRA assumption), credit hygiene (lower reported utilization without closing needed cards; 30% is a heuristic; no credit-repair pitch), and a Big-5 package exit that leaves the mortgage in place (90-day overlap, no-fee chequing, written zero balance; not a mortgage-rate shop). Education only — not tax, deposit, credit, or legal advice. No invented search volumes. - [Transfer to a parent](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/transfer-tuition-credit-to-parent-canada.html) — Transferring the tuition amount in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026: the student must file a return and use the tuition amount first to reduce their own federal tax to zero; they can then transfer up to $5,000 of the current-year federal tuition amount, minus what they used, to a parent or grandparent (theirs or their spouse's) or to a spouse or common-law partner; designated on Schedule 11 and the T2202 or provincial forms; the receiving person claims it on line 32400 (parent or grandparent) or through Schedule 2 (spouse); carry-forward amounts cannot be transferred; the student must claim them in the first year they have income tax to pay and must file a return every year to keep them (a missed year means the amount is not carried forward); federal value is the lowest-rate credit (14.5% for 2025, 14% for 2026), so $5,000 is worth up to $725 for 2025 or $700 for 2026; Ontario ended its provincial tuition credit in 2017; eligible fees generally over $100 per institution; made-up worked example.
- [RRSP for school](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/lifelong-learning-plan-rrsp-withdraw-school-canada.html) — Lifelong Learning Plan (LLP) in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026: withdraw up to $10,000 per calendar year and $20,000 in total from your RRSPs for full-time training or education for you or your spouse or common-law partner, using Form RC96 for each withdrawal; not taxed and no withholding if the conditions are met; repay at least one-tenth a year over 10 years (for example $2,000 a year on $20,000), designated on Schedule 7; repayment generally starts in the fifth year after your first withdrawal, or usually earlier if the student is not a qualifying student for at least three months in each of two years in a row; any shortfall is added to income that year; RRSP contributions made in the 89-day period before a withdrawal may not be deductible; if the student leaves before April of the year after the withdrawal and 75% or more of tuition is refundable, the withdrawal must be cancelled (repaid, Form RC97) or it is included in income; compared with interest-free federal student loans, regular RRSP withdrawals with withholding tax (10%, 20%, 30% outside Quebec) and RESPs; made-up worked example.
- [Grace period and RAP](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/student-loan-repayment-canada-grace-period-rap.html) — Student loan repayment in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026: Canada Student Loans are interest-free (federal interest permanently eliminated in 2023); repayment starts after a six-month grace period after you leave full-time studies; provincial portions differ, and Ontario and Saskatchewan are the only provinces charging interest on their portion (Ontario at prime plus 1%, including during the grace period), per CBC News, 25 Aug 2026; the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) lowers or pauses payments based on family income and size, with periods of six months and reapplication; canada.ca lists monthly gross family income thresholds below which you may not need to pay for 6 months: $3,866 for a family of 1, $4,535 for 2, $5,556 for 3 and $6,412 for 4 (thresholds may differ for the provincial part); RAP requires loans in repayment and payments up to date; student loan interest tax credit on line 31900 for interest on government student loans, carry forward five years; per canada.ca, after 9 months of missed payments the federal part goes to the CRA for collections, with no access to student aid until the loan is back in good standing, and missing payments affects your credit; made-up repayment plan.
- [Funerals and the CPP death benefit](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/funeral-costs-cpp-death-benefit-canada.html) — Funeral costs and the CPP death benefit in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026: the CPP death benefit is a one-time $2,500 payment to the estate or eligible applicants when the deceased made enough CPP contributions; for deaths on or after 1 Jan 2025 a $2,500 top-up (total $5,000) is possible when the deceased never received a CPP or QPP retirement pension, disability benefit or post-retirement disability benefit and has no surviving spouse or common-law partner eligible for a survivor's pension (canada.ca); the executor should apply within 60 days of the death, and if there is no estate or the executor has not applied, payment may go to the person or institution that paid for the funeral, then the surviving spouse or common-law partner, then next of kin; payment takes about 6 to 12 weeks; the CRA says it is reported on the T3 return if one is filed for the estate, otherwise by a beneficiary on line 13000; the CPP survivor's pension is separate; Ontario funeral providers must give price lists before a contract, buyers get a full refund within 30 days of signing, and cancellation fees after 30 days are capped at 10% or $350 (ontario.ca); prepaid contracts guaranteed since 1 July 2012; Ontario estate administration tax $15 per $1,000 over $50,000; cost items, direct cremation versus full service; made-up budget example.

- [StudentAid BC 2026-27](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/studentaid-bc-2026-27-grants-loans.html) — StudentAid BC 2026-27, as of 1 Oct 2026: Canada-B.C. integrated loans administered as one loan; B.C. and Canada student loans are interest-free; minimum 60% course load (40% with a permanent or persistent or prolonged disability); repayment starts on the 1st day of the 7th month after studies end; NSLSC messages about 45 days before. B.C. Access Grant full-time (B.C. public schools, undergraduate, at least $1 assessed need, automatic): up to $4,000 per 8-month year ($117.65 a week) for programs under 2 years, up to $1,000 ($29.41 a week) for 2+ years; no grant at family income of $80,491 (1 person) for under-2-year programs or $48,978 (1 person) for 2+ year programs. Part-time Access Grant up to $1,000 a year, cut-off $55,981 for 1 person. Paid in full up front for study periods of 17 weeks or less, otherwise half at start and half at midpoint. Federal 2026-27: full-time grant $525 a month, weekly loan limit $300. BCAG-D replaces up to $1,560 of B.C. loan. B.C. Loan Forgiveness: up to 20% a year for 5 years of the B.C. portion.
- [Alberta Student Aid 2026-27](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/alberta-student-aid-2026-27-grants-loans.html) — Alberta Student Aid 2026-27, as of 1 Oct 2026: one application assesses Alberta and Canada aid; calculated need = allowable costs minus resources; amounts apply from 1 Aug 2026. Eligibility: citizen, PR or protected person, Alberta resident, 60% course load (40% with a disability); study-permit holders not eligible. Most applications processed within 30 days, manual review up to 45; apply 60 days ahead. Combined loan limits: $8,500 a semester, $17,000 for two, $25,500 for three; lifetime limits from $51,000 (one-year programs) to $200,000 (medicine, dentistry, etc.). Alberta Student Grant for Full-time Students up to $425 a month (one-year programs, apprenticeship, graduate) at incomes up to the federal thresholds ($38,474 for 1). Canada Student Grant full-time $525 a month, no grant at $69,987 (1 person); dependants $280 per dependant per month, no grant at $98,017 (family of 2). From 1 Aug 2026 the full-time federal grant is limited to public and not-for-profit private institutions. Grace: Alberta loans 12 months, Canada 6 months; Alberta interest at CIBC prime (floating or one-time fixed) since 1 Jul 2023; no interest on Canada loans. Alberta terms: up to $3,000 over 3 years, $3,001-$6,000 over 8, $6,001+ over 9.5.
- [Quebec AFE loans and bursaries](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/quebec-afe-loans-bursaries-guide.html) — Quebec Aide financière aux études (AFE) Loans and Bursaries Program, as of 1 Oct 2026: for full-time vocational, college and university students; you receive a loan first, and a bursary (not repaid) if need exceeds the loan amount set for your level of education. Government pays loan interest during full-time studies; 6 months before repayment after studies; non-refundable tax credit on interest paid. Parent or sponsor contribution required unless the student is self-supporting (e.g., parent of a child or at least 20 weeks pregnant, 24 months self-supporting or working without full-time study, 7 years since compulsory schooling without full-time study, 90 university credits in Quebec, bachelor's degree, or full-time master's/doctoral); spouse's income counts if married, in a civil union or living together with a child. Allowable expenses include tuition, books and supplies, living costs and childcare; $500 per term training materials allowance as a loan. Apply from about May; within 30 days after your last month of study in the school year (1 Sep-31 Aug); documents within 45 days; all by 29 Dec. Loan Remission Program: 15% off for finishing on time with a bursary each award year; apply within 3 years; not taxable.
- [Part-time student grant](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/canada-student-grant-part-time-2026-27.html) — Canada Student Grant for Part-Time Students 2026-27, as of 1 Oct 2026: up to $2,520 for the school year (1 Aug 2026-31 Jul 2027), set by SOR/2026-139; never more than assessed need (e.g., $1,200 need gives $1,200). Part-time need is allowable educational costs only; living costs and resources are not counted. Full grant at or below family income of $38,474 (1 person), $54,412 (2), $66,641 (3), $76,952 (4), $86,033 (5), $94,245 (6), $101,797 (7+); no grant at or above $69,987, $98,017, $117,317, $129,769, $141,180, $151,937, $161,321. Phase-out: about 8 cents per dollar above the threshold for 1 person (annual rate 0.079968). Must have completed courses previously funded. Not for students from NWT, Nunavut or Quebec. Part-time loans up to the lesser of need or a $10,000 maximum outstanding balance. Part-time students with dependants: separate grant up to $2,688. B.C. adds a part-time Access Grant of up to $1,000.
- [Grants for students with disabilities](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/canada-student-grant-students-with-disabilities.html) — Canada Student Grant for Students with Disabilities, 2026-27, as of 1 Oct 2026: $2,800 per program year (1 Aug-31 Jul), set by SOR/2026-139; StudentAid BC says the amount is temporarily 40% above 2019-20 levels until 31 Jul 2027. Full- or part-time students with a permanent, or persistent or prolonged, disability who qualify for a federal loan; Gazette says it goes to all students with disabilities who have assessed need; 11% of program students identified as having a disability in 2023-24. Canada Student Grant for Services and Equipment: up to $20,000 per loan year for exceptional education-related services and equipment such as tutors, note-takers, interpreters and technical aids. Disability status allows full-time funding at a 40% to 59% load (B.C., Alberta). StudentAid BC: status takes about 6 weeks; persistent or prolonged status must be redone at repayment or after a 5-year break. B.C. Access Grant for Students with Disabilities replaces up to $1,560 of B.C. loan. RAP-D: government pays principal and interest not covered; maximum 10 years in repayment; no restriction on future aid.
- [Grants for students with dependants](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/canada-student-grant-students-with-dependants.html) — Canada Student Grant for Full-Time Students with Dependants, 2026-27, as of 1 Oct 2026: up to $280 per dependant per month of study (SOR/2026-139), on top of the full-time grant; about $2,240 per dependant over an 8-month year. Dependant: under 12 at the start of the study period, or over 12 with a permanent disability (canada.ca); Alberta also lists 12-18 with a permanent disability and wholly dependent family members. Maximum at or below family income of $54,412 (family of 2), $66,641 (3), $76,952 (4), $86,033 (5), $94,245 (6), $101,797 (7+); cut off at $98,017, $117,317, $129,769, $141,180, $151,937, $161,321 (Alberta 2026-27 table). Monthly phase-out rates per dollar above the threshold, family of 2 to 7+: 0.006421282, 0.005525296, 0.005301324, 0.005077338, 0.004853366, 0.004703986. Part-time students with dependants: up to $2,688 for 2026-27. Not for students from NWT, Nunavut or Quebec.
- [RAP: how much you pay](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/repayment-assistance-plan-how-much-pay-canada.html) — Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP), as of 1 Oct 2026: monthly gross family income thresholds on canada.ca by family size 1-7: $3,866, $4,535, $5,556, $6,412, $7,170, $7,854, $8,483; at or below, the federal payment is $0 for 6 months. Above it, the Canada Student Financial Assistance Regulations s.19 set the monthly affordable payment as family income times the lesser of 0.1A and 1.5[(X-Y)/100Z + 0.01]A, so it starts near 1.5% of family income just above the threshold and is capped at 10% (A = share of family student debt). Reapply every 6 months; must be in repayment 6+ months, live in Canada, be up to date. Government pays unpaid federal interest; pays principal after 60 months of RAP or 10 years after school; maximum repayment 15 years (10 with a disability). After government pays principal, no new grants or loans until repaid (not RAP-D). Apply at NSLSC; PEI borrowers also apply provincially.

- [Free online courses](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/free-online-courses-canada-library-linkedin-learning.html) — Free online courses through Canadian public libraries, as of 1 Oct 2026: Toronto Public Library card gives free LinkedIn Learning (thousands of courses; some in French and other languages), instructor-led courses with certificates of completion, IT skills courses, interactive courses in 71 languages, test prep (LSAT, MCAT, SAT, GMAT, GRE, TOEIC, TOEFL, citizenship), Road to IELTS and Brainfuse live help. Calgary Public Library: LinkedIn Learning with card number and PIN; certificates do not show your name; library version not linked to personal LinkedIn; membership free to Calgary residents and surrounding Indigenous communities. Vancouver and Ottawa public libraries also offer LinkedIn Learning. Canada training credit (CRA): $250 a year added to your limit if eligible, up to $5,000 lifetime; ages 26 to 65 at year end; claim the lesser of your limit and 50% of eligible tuition at eligible institutions; refundable.
- [Canada training credit](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/canada-training-credit-how-to-claim.html) — Canada training credit (CTC), from the CRA line 45350 page and Guide P105 for 2025, as of 1 Oct 2026: refundable credit for eligible tuition and fees; claim the lesser of your Canada training credit limit (CTCL) and 50% of eligible fees on Schedule 11; enter line 5 of Schedule 11 on line 45350. Room: $250 a year if you qualify, $5,000 lifetime. To accumulate $250 for 2026 you must, in 2025, file a return, be resident in Canada all year, be at least 26 and under 66 at year end, have at least $12,058 of working income (including maternity and parental benefits) and net income not above $177,882. CTCL = previous limit + $250 accumulation − CTC claimed last year. Limit shown on notice of assessment. Exam fees for occupational, trade or professional exams can count. Fees over $100 per institution.
- [Student loan interest credit](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/student-loan-interest-tax-credit-line-31900.html) — Student loan interest credit (line 31900 federal, line 58520 provincial), from the CRA and NSLSC, as of 1 Oct 2026: claim interest paid on loans under the Canada Student Loans Act, Canada Student Financial Assistance Act, Apprentice Loans Act or similar provincial laws; only the borrower can claim, even if a parent paid; no fixed federal maximum; carry forward unused interest up to five years, oldest first; cannot claim interest on loans combined, renegotiated or consolidated with a bank, non-government loans, or court-judgment interest; cannot transfer. NSLSC: interest on all Canada Student Loans permanently eliminated from 1 April 2023; interest accrues only on the provincial portions of Canada-Ontario (floating prime + 1.0%) and Canada-Saskatchewan (floating prime) integrated loans; no interest on BC, NL, MB, NB portions; Alberta, Nova Scotia and PEI loans are separate payments. NSLSC issues an income tax receipt for interest paid each year.
- [Student moving expenses](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/student-moving-expenses-deduction-line-21900.html) — Student moving expenses (line 21900), from the CRA moving expenses page and Guide P105 for 2025, as of 1 Oct 2026: if your tuition form shows full-time enrolment (box C), you can claim moving expenses for a move to attend post-secondary school, deductible only from the taxable part of scholarships, bursaries, fellowships, certain prizes and research grants; or for a move to work (including summer jobs, self-employment, or returning to school after a co-op work term), deductible only from employment or self-employment income at the new location. New home must be at least 40 km closer by the shortest public route. Unused amounts carry forward against the same type of income; no carry back. Eligible: transportation and storage, travel (vehicle and meals, detailed or simplified method), up to 15 days of temporary living, lease cancellation, incidental costs. Not eligible: house-hunting trips, mail forwarding, cleaning a rental to the landlord's standard. Separate Form T1-M per move. Employer-paid expenses not claimable unless included in income.
- [Exam fees and the tuition credit](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/professional-exam-fees-tuition-tax-credit-cpa.html) — Professional exam fees and the tuition tax credit, from the CRA and CPA Ontario, as of 1 Oct 2026: exam fees paid to an educational institution, professional association, provincial ministry or similar body to take an occupational, trade or professional exam required for professional status recognized by federal or provincial statute, or to be licensed or certified as a tradesperson, may be eligible; ancillary fees over $250 for an exam are not eligible unless required of all candidates; receipt should certify the eligible amount under paragraph 118.5(1)(d); entrance fees to professional organizations and exam fees not integral to a program are not eligible. Exam fees can also count for the Canada training credit. CPA Ontario 2026 (plus HST): Core 1 $1,525; other PEP modules $1,450 each; exam only $550; CFE all three days $2,050; Day 1 $915; Days 2 and 3 $1,600; annual student dues $725 standard, $365 undergraduate/co-op. CPA Ontario says all certification program courses, exams and rewrite fees are eligible for the T2202; materials and administrative fees are not; courses are part-time, two months each; Ontario eliminated its tuition credit effective 4 Sep 2017. Federal tuition transfer up to $5,000.
- [Private school tuition and tax](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/private-school-tuition-tax-deductible-canada.html) — Private school tuition and tax in Canada, from the CRA, as of 1 Oct 2026: the tuition tax credit covers courses at post-secondary institutions, or occupational skills courses at certified institutions for people 16 or older, so regular elementary and secondary tuition is not eligible. Child care expense deduction (line 21400): can include the part of fees to educational institutions that relates to child care services, and boarding schools, overnight sports schools or camps where lodging is involved (see note in Part A of Form T778); cannot include tuition fees of a regular program or a sports study program; child under 16 at some time in the year or with an infirmity; usually claimed by the lower-income spouse. Religious schools (IC75-23): payments to a registered charity school that teaches exclusively religion may be receipted as donations; for schools offering both secular and religious education, only the part above the net secular (or whole-school) cost per pupil can be receipted. Medical expense credit: school for persons with a mental or physical impairment, if an appropriately qualified person certifies in writing that the school's specially provided equipment, facilities or staff are needed.
- [Better Jobs Ontario](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/better-jobs-ontario-funding-retraining.html) — Better Jobs Ontario, from ontario.ca (updated 25 Sep 2026), as of 1 Oct 2026: skills training for in-demand jobs plus financial support; short-term programs of 52 weeks or less (including micro-credentials) and programs up to 2 years. Up to $28,000 for training of 1 year or less; up to $35,000 for programs over 1 year and up to 2 years. Covers tuition, books, other instructional costs (student fees, supplies, electronic devices), transportation and a basic living allowance up to $500 a week; extra funding may be available for child care, disability supports, living away from home, literacy and essential skills (Get Set) and language training. Eligible if laid off and not working, laid off and in a temporary job to cover costs, or not laid off but unemployed 12 weeks or longer and in a low-income household; EI, Ontario Works and ODSP recipients can apply. Apply through an Employment Ontario service provider; research at least 3 institutions including at least one public college and one career college (only 1 if self-funded); funding based on needs and available funding; supports the most cost-effective options. CRA: fees paid by a government job training program cannot be claimed for the tuition credit unless included in income.
- [EI and going back to school](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/ei-going-back-to-school-approved-training.html) — EI while in training, from ESDC and Service Canada pages, as of 1 Oct 2026: declare training before it starts. Non-referred training (chosen without approval from Service Canada, a province or territory, or an Indigenous organization): must remain capable and available, keep looking for suitable work, and be ready to change or cancel training for a job. Referred training: approved by a designated authority; Service Canada may refer you if you receive or are eligible for regular or fishing benefits, are approved for a program at a designated or certified institution in Canada, are full-time as defined by the institution, pay for the training yourself, and are a long-tenured worker (fewer than 36 weeks of regular or fishing benefits in the 3 years before the claim, and paid at least 30% of the annual maximum EI premiums in 7 of the last 10 years). Provinces, territories and Indigenous organizations can also refer EI clients. Benefits are not extended to cover longer training. Apprentices: 16-digit reference code for each block of full-time technical training; 1-week waiting period served once per apprenticeship. EI 2026: 55% of average insurable weekly earnings, maximum insurable earnings $68,900, maximum $729 a week, 14 to 45 weeks.
- [Apprenticeship costs](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/skilled-trades-apprenticeship-cost-canada-apprentice-loan.html) — Apprenticeship costs and supports in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Canada Apprentice Loan (ESDC, CALSC): up to $4,000 interest-free per period of technical training, up to 5 periods, Red Seal trades only, not available in Quebec; no payments or interest until you complete or leave training; payment-free for up to 312 weeks (6 years) while registered; credit check for first-time applicants; not if receiving a Canada Student Loan for the same training. Apprenticeship Incentive Grant: $1,000 per year or level after completing the first or second year/level in a Red Seal trade (up to $2,000), taxable. Apprenticeship Completion Grant: $2,000 lifetime, taxable. EI: regular benefits during referred full-time technical training; 16-digit reference code per block; 1-week waiting period once per apprenticeship. Tradesperson's tools deduction (CRA, 2024 page): lesser of $1,000 and (cost of eligible tools minus $1,433), employer certifies on T2200; GST/HST rebate possible. Ontario: Tools Grant $1,000 motive power, $600 construction or industrial, $400 service (taxable; after level one since 1 Apr 2020, 12 months registered); Apprentice Development Benefit during full-time in-class training; Apprenticeship Completion Bonus $2,000 for non-Red Seal trades.
- [University without an RESP](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/pay-for-university-without-resp-canada.html) — Paying for university without an RESP, as of 1 Oct 2026. CESG (ESDC): 20% of the first $2,500 a year (up to $500), extra $100 or $50 for low and middle incomes, $7,200 lifetime; unused room carries forward so up to $1,000 a year on $5,000; available until the end of the year the child turns 17; at 16 or 17 only if $2,000 was contributed before the end of the year they turned 15, or $100 a year in any four earlier years. Canada Learning Bond: up to $2,000 for low-income families, no contributions needed, request by the day before age 21 (born 2004 or later). TFSA (CRA): 2026 dollar limit $7,000; withdrawals restore room on 1 January of the next year. Federal student aid 2026-27 (SOR/2026-139): Canada Student Grant for full-time students up to $525 per month of study; weekly federal loan limit $300. NSLSC: Canada Student Loans interest-free since 1 April 2023; repayment starts the first day of the 7th month after studies end. CRA: full-time post-secondary scholarships and bursaries not taxable; student may transfer up to $5,000 of current-year federal tuition amount (minus what they use) to a parent or grandparent.
- [University meal plans](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/university-meal-plan-cost-canada-worth-it.html) — University residence meal plans 2026-27, as of 1 Oct 2026. McMaster: mandatory for all residence students, no exemptions except rare cases with a physician or religious leader's note; Traditional plans A-D total $7,280, $7,510, $7,740, $7,960 (4-month $3,640-$3,980); Apartment plans A-D $4,590, $4,830, $5,070, $5,310; totals include a $50 administration charge and a $185 capital improvement charge; each purchase draws 50% from the Basic bucket and 50% from an Overhead bucket; unused Basic carries forward to end of enrolment, Overhead does not; default C plan if no choice; change deadline 4 Aug 2026; Basic portion tax-exempt. Western: Plan 1 $8,300 (food credit $4,100 = $3,550 residence dollars + $550 flex; overhead $4,050; capital improvement $150); Plan 2 $7,700 (food credit $3,500; same overhead and capital fee). University of Ottawa: mandatory 5-day plan $7,125 in 2026-27 (was $6,825 in 2025-26) in traditional residences and some suites. CRA: board and lodging are not eligible tuition fees.
- [Eid budget 2027](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/eid-budget-canada-2027.html) — Eid budget Canada 2027, as of 1 Oct 2026. Fiqh Council of North America (FCNA) calculated calendar: Ramadan 1448 begins Monday 8 February 2027; Eid al-Fitr (1 Shawwal 1448) Tuesday 9 March 2027; Dhul-Hijjah 1448 begins Friday 7 May 2027; FCNA says Eid al-Adha is the day after the Day of Arafah as determined by Saudi Arabia's Supreme Court. Many mosques use local moon sighting, so dates can differ by a day. Statistics Canada 2023 average household spending (table 11-10-0222-01): food from stores $8,579, restaurant food $3,316, clothing and accessories $2,716, gifts of money to people in Canada $386 and outside Canada $185, charitable contributions $671. CRA: donation credits need an official receipt from a qualified donee; non-refundable; up to 75% of net income; carry forward 5 years; spouses can pool. Zakat al-Fitr amounts are set per person by your mosque or zakat organization.

Royal Observatory Greenwich: Western Easter Sunday 2027 is 28 March; Eastern Orthodox Easter can fall on the same day or one, four or five weeks later. Good Friday 2027 is 26 March (two days before). Ontario's Employment Standards Act lists Good Friday among nine public holidays. Statistics Canada 2023 average household spending (table 11-10-0222-01): food from stores $8,579, restaurant food $3,316, clothing and accessories $2,716. Tips: set a per-child basket cap, buy chocolate and decor after Easter for next year, host a potluck dinner, and use free community egg hunts.
- [Graduation party and gifts](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/graduation-party-gifts-cost-canada.html) — Graduation party and gift costs in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Guest count drives cost; a backyard or home party is cheapest. AGCO (Ontario): you do not need a special occasion permit to serve alcohol to invited guests in your own home or a private place (an indoor place the public would not normally be and that is not rented to the public); a permit is needed if alcohol is sold, and private events with invited guests only can use a private event permit; a venue's own licence may cover the event. CRA: TFSA contribution room starts at 18 for Canadian residents; the 2026 TFSA dollar limit is $7,000. Statistics Canada 2023: average household gifts of money to people in Canada $386. Gift amounts in examples are made up; there is no official guideline.

- [Used road bike buying](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/used-road-bike-buying-canada.html) — Buying a used road bike in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Check the serial number against stolen-bike reports, for example 529 Garage's Check a Bike search; the serial is usually etched or stamped on the bottom bracket shell, otherwise look on the seat tube, crank, under the top tube or on the head tube. Toronto Police: register your bike, engrave an identifying number if there is no serial, use a hardened steel U-lock or a hardened steel chain and padlock, and lock the frame and both wheels to an immovable object. Ontario requires a bell or horn, a white front light and a red rear light or reflector at night, white reflective tape on the front forks and red on the rear forks; helmets are required by law under 18 and strongly recommended but not legally required for 18 and over. Budget for a tune-up, lock, lights and fit adjustments on top of the price.

National Ballet of Canada: subscribers save up to 50% compared with single tickets; build-your-own packages of 3, 4 or 5 ballets save up to 10%, 12% or 15%; free exchanges with at least 24 hours' notice; payment plans; subscriber discount card. Canadian Opera Company: full-season subscription has free ticket exchanges and highest seating priority; smaller 4- and 3-opera packages have a discounted exchange fee; all subscribers get a discount on additional tickets. Toronto Symphony Orchestra: TSOUNDCHECK (ages 15 to 35) Pick 5 subscriptions from $27 per ticket Main Floor or $35 Mezzanine, saving 20% compared with TSOUNDCHECK single prices, fee-free exchanges (normally $10 per ticket with 48 hours' notice), and 20% off regular single tickets for extra concerts. A subscription is worth it if you would attend most of the shows anyway and value exchanges and seat priority.

- [Cancelled or postponed concert refunds](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/concert-cancelled-postponed-refund-canada.html) — Concert cancelled or postponed refunds in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Ticketmaster Canada: event organizers set refund policies; when refunds are offered a Request Refund button appears under My Tickets; refunds go to the original payment method and should appear in 5 to 7 business days depending on the bank; transfer recipients contact the original point of purchase. Ticketmaster help centre: postponed means the organizer is still deciding whether to reschedule or cancel and tickets stay valid; rescheduled or moved events keep tickets valid for the new date, and the organizer may offer refunds; box office buyers contact the box office. Ontario Ticket Sales Act: resale buyers must get written validation or a written money-back guarantee, including a refund if the event is cancelled before the ticket can be used; complaints go to Consumer Protection Ontario. Hotel, flight and parking costs are separate bookings with their own cancellation rules.
- [Dynamic ticket pricing explained](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/dynamic-pricing-concert-tickets-canada.html) — Dynamic pricing for concert tickets in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Ticketmaster Canada: event organizers set ticket face value and can change it at any time; Ticketmaster keeps no part of face value; Platinum tickets are popular seats sold at a price set by the event organizer, which Ticketmaster says does not use algorithmic surge pricing technology; Platinum is not a VIP package and can be resold subject to event terms. Fees: per-ticket service fee, per-order processing fee, optional delivery fee and a facility charge set by the venue. Ontario Ticket Sales Act: primary sellers must disclose capacity and how tickets are distributed, including pre-sales; show the total price in Canadian dollars with fees itemized; print the total on the ticket; resale is capped at the original total plus taxes and the platform's standard fees; bots are banned. Competition Bureau: advertising a price that cannot be attained because of mandatory fixed fees is against the law, except government-imposed amounts such as sales tax.
- [Scene+ points for movies](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/scene-plus-points-movies-maximize-canada.html) — Scene+ points for movies, as of 1 Oct 2026. Scene+ help centre: earn 3 to 6 points per $1 on eligible Cineplex movie tickets and concessions, possibly more with a qualifying Scotiabank credit card; points usually appear within 48 hours. Redeem 100 points for $1 toward movie tickets, food or drinks, or 500 points for $5 off other eligible purchases; redemptions cannot be applied to taxes, gratuities or alcohol; points can also buy Cineplex gift cards. Rec Room and Playdium earn 1 point per $1. Cineplex deals page: Big Deal Tuesdays with an extra 10% off Tuesday prices for Scene+ members; limited-time 5x points on premium tickets. Comparison: Sobeys groceries 1,000 points for $10; Scotiabank travel 100 points for $1; Points for Credit 150 points for $1. Registered accounts close after 24 months of inactivity and points are forfeited.

- [Is ticket insurance worth it?](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/ticket-insurance-worth-it-canada.html) — Ticket insurance in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Ticketmaster Canada offers Allianz Event Ticket Protector, underwritten by CUMIS General Insurance Company and administered by Allianz Global Assistance. Ticketmaster says it reimburses 100% of the ticket price including taxes and shipping when you cannot attend for a covered reason. Policy wording: reimburses non-refundable ticket costs for tickets bought through a primary outlet when you cannot attend for a Covered Reason; does not cover a personal change in plans; benefit maximums of $1,000 each for ticket cost, reissuing fees and change fees. Covered reasons include unforeseen serious illness or injury (physician exam within 48 hours), death of a family member within 30 days, common-carrier delays, traffic accidents en route, layoff after 3 years with an employer, jury duty, home made uninhabitable within 72 hours, car breakdown within 48 hours, and an event cancelled and not rescheduled or refunded. Exclusions include pre-existing conditions (90-day look-back), business obligations, foreseeable events and epidemics or pandemics. Full refund of premium within 10 days if no claim and the event has not passed.

- [Access 2 Card](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/access-2-card-free-support-person-ticket-canada.html) — Access 2 Card, as of 1 Oct 2026. Run by Easter Seals Canada since 2004 with over 500 movie theatres, cultural attractions, entertainment venues and recreation facilities across Canada. The cardholder (person with a permanent disability) pays regular admission and their support person gets free admission. Eligibility: permanent disability that requires a support person at participating venues; support person must be 18 or older, may be related and need not be a PSW unless the venue says so; all ages. Application: Section C completed by one of 12 listed health care professionals or a disability service organization's executive director (not related); CNIB card accepted instead. Administration fee on the application page: $25 for a new 3-year card, $35 for a new 5-year card (an Easter Seals page lists $20 and $30). Allow up to four weeks. Physical card must be shown. Online or advance tickets usually not possible; Cineplex and Landmark do not allow online tickets with the card. If the cardholder is admitted free because of age, the card cannot be used.

- [Ontario fishing licence cost](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/ontario-fishing-licence-cost-outdoors-card.html) — Ontario fishing licence fees for 2026 (in effect until 31 Dec 2026), from ontario.ca, as of 1 Oct 2026, plus 13% HST. Outdoors Card $8.57, valid 3 calendar years; renewal period starts the first Tuesday of December. A new licensing system replaces the Fish and Wildlife Licensing Service in early 2027.
- [Hiking gear budget](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/hiking-gear-budget-canada.html) — Hiking gear budget for Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. AdventureSmart (a national search and rescue prevention program) lists ten essentials for any outdoor trip: flashlight with spare batteries, fire-making kit, signalling device such as a whistle or mirror, extra food and water (1 litre per person), extra clothing (rain, wind and a toque), navigation and communication aids (at minimum a map and compass), first aid kit, emergency shelter such as an orange tarp, pocket knife, and sun protection. It also recommends leaving a trip plan and dressing in base, mid and outer layers. Parks Canada 2026: Banff daily admission $12.25 adult, $10.75 senior, $24.50 family or group; Discovery Pass $83.50 adult, $167.50 family or group of up to seven in one vehicle; youth 17 and under free. Gear prices in the example are made up.
- [Used golf clubs and fitting](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/used-golf-clubs-fitting-canada.html) — Used golf clubs and fitting in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Golf Town pre-owned clubs are inspected for authenticity and condition at head, shaft and grip; 38 certified pre-owned locations. Trade-ins: appraised in store using Golf99 or a similar price guide; value must go to a new club purchase of equal or greater price; no cash; junior clubs not eligible; cracked or bent shafts, chrome damage and excessive wear are refused. Trade-In Event 17 Sep to 28 Oct 2026: 50% bonus on trade value toward select new drivers, woods and iron sets from listed brands; iron sets need at least 5 consecutive clubs; one bonus per transaction. Sample listed trade values (men's right hand, regular shaft, good condition): Titleist TSi2 driver $182, PING G425 Max driver $282, PING G425 7-piece steel irons $402, Odyssey Eleven S putter $97. Vendor Fitting Days cost $59.99, waived with a club purchase over $549. Rules of Golf Rule 4.1b: no more than 14 clubs.
- [Sports for adults 55+](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/seniors-sports-55-plus-games-canada.html) — Sports for adults 55 and older in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Ontario 55+ Games are provincial competitions delivered by Games Ontario; Summer Games in odd years and Winter Games in even years; participation begins at a local Ontario Senior Games Association district; sports include badminton, curling, darts, hockey, pickleball, swimming and walking. Games Ontario lists the 2028 Ontario 55+ Winter Games in Orillia, dates to be announced. 55+ BC Games fees at a glance: membership $20, participant registration $100, plus event fees such as pickleball $30, hockey $30, ice curling $25, swimming $15, golf $143. City of Toronto: all drop-in skating is free, with Older Adult (60+) sessions; leisure swim is free at all pools; Older Adult lane swim is free; adults 60+ get 50% off registered adult programs (private and small group lessons excluded).
- [Student line of credit vs loan](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/student-line-of-credit-vs-government-student-loan-canada.html) — Student line of credit versus government student loan in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. FCAC: since 1 April 2023, Canada Student Loans accumulate no interest, including loans in repayment; provincial portions may still accrue interest depending on the province (NSLSC lists the Ontario portion at floating prime plus 1%; BC, Newfoundland and Labrador, Manitoba and New Brunswick portions carry no interest). Canada Student Loans have a 6-month non-repayment period after graduation and access to the Repayment Assistance Plan; lines of credit do not. Student lines of credit: borrow up to a limit, pay interest only on what you use, and must pay at least the interest while studying; most lenders allow interest-only payments for a grace period, usually 6 to 12 months after graduation. You may need a co-signer. Lenders cannot require optional credit insurance. TD Student Line of Credit: no co-signer needed to apply (assessed case by case), interest-only while in school, no principal payments until 24 months after leaving school; cash offer of $300, $550 or $1,000 if approved by 31 Oct 2026.
- [Co-signing a student loan](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/co-sign-student-loan-parent-canada-risks.html) — Co-signing a student loan or line of credit in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. FCAC: a joint borrower is someone who signs a loan, credit card or line of credit agreement with others, also called co-signing; each becomes equally responsible for repaying the unpaid balance. With a federally regulated lender, every joint borrower has the right to the cost disclosure and the same ongoing statements, unless they consent otherwise. FCAC's student line of credit page says you may need someone, like a parent, to co-sign, and that person is responsible for the debt if the student cannot pay. Lenders cannot require optional credit insurance. TD says co-signer requirements for its Student Line of Credit are assessed case by case based on credit history. Canada Student Loans accumulate no interest since 1 April 2023 and include the Repayment Assistance Plan.
- [Gift or loan to an adult child](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/parents-paying-adult-child-university-gift-or-loan.html) — Paying for an adult child's university in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. CRA lists most gifts and inheritances among amounts that are not reported or taxed. Income Tax Act s. 74.1(2): income from property transferred or lent to a non-arm's-length person under 18 (or a niece or nephew) is attributed back to the transferor. For adult children, s. 56(4.1) can attribute income from property bought with a low-interest or interest-free loan back to the lender when one of the main reasons for the loan was to reduce or avoid tax by moving income. CRA: a student can transfer up to $5,000 of the current year's federal tuition amount (minus what they use) to a parent or grandparent using Schedule 11; the parent claims it on line 32400. FCAC: a co-signer is equally responsible for the whole unpaid balance. Canada Student Loans accumulate no interest since 1 April 2023.

- [Exchange semester costs](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/exchange-semester-abroad-cost-canada.html) — Exchange semester abroad costs for Canadian students, as of 1 Oct 2026. Queen's University: while on exchange you continue to pay tuition to Queen's and remain registered; apply for the Exchange Bursary. University of Waterloo: on exchange, tuition is assessed at Waterloo for the term (charged for 2.5 units whatever the course load abroad) plus compulsory incidental fees. OSAP for exchange (University of Toronto guide): available for a U of T exchange with transfer credits; covers educational costs at standard allowances but not the extra costs of going abroad; you are assessed as living away from home; 60% course load (40% with a disability); exchange terms count toward program length plus one year. OHIP: you can keep coverage while studying full time outside Canada if you have a valid health card, have been in Ontario at least 153 days in each of the two 12-month periods before leaving, and Ontario is your primary home; apply for an academic absence at ServiceOntario. OHIP pays up to $50 a day for emergency outpatient care and up to $400 a day for intensive inpatient care abroad ($200 lower levels); Ontario recommends travel medical insurance. travel.gc.ca: provincial plans may cover none or only a small part of costs abroad and never pay up front.

- [Special occasion permits](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/special-occasion-permit-ontario-cost.html) — Ontario special occasion permits (AGCO), as of 1 Oct 2026. No permit needed to serve alcohol to invited guests in your own home or a private place (an indoor place not normally open to the public and not rented out to the public). A permit is needed for private events elsewhere unless the venue's liquor sales licence covers the event. Private event permits: no-sale permit $50 per day (free drinks, no admission or tickets); sale permit $150 per day (cash bar, drink tickets, admission fees; money only toward the cost of alcohol). Liquor cannot be sold at a residence. Hours 9 a.m. to 2 a.m. (3 a.m. on New Year's Eve). Outdoor events need notification letters to municipal authorities 30 to 60 days before; capacity 12 square feet (1.11 square metres) per person outdoors. Usually one day to approve, up to 10 days; apply at least 10 days ahead through iAGCO. Public event permits are also $50 or $150 per day.

- [Prepaid funeral plans in Ontario](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/prepaid-funeral-plan-ontario-protections.html) — Prepaid funeral plans in Ontario, as of 1 Oct 2026 (ontario.ca). You can preplan without prepaying; most providers keep a record of plans without cost. Two ways to prepay: money held in trust by a bank, trust company or independent trustee, which must be in very safe investments and earns income to offset price increases (you can ask once a year where it is invested and how much is in trust); or insurance, which requires two contracts and is protected under the Insurance Act. Prepayments to licensed funeral establishments or transfer services are protected by the Prepaid Funeral Services Compensation Fund administered by the Bereavement Authority of Ontario. Since 1 July 2012 prepaid contracts must be guaranteed. Cancel any time in writing: full refund within 30 days of signing; after 30 days a provider may keep 10% of the amount in trust, up to $350. Leftover money goes to the estate or a named person for funeral and transfer contracts signed on or after 1 June 1990 and cemetery or crematorium contracts on or after 1 April 1992. The example amounts are made up.

- [Wedding officiant fees](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/wedding-officiant-fees-canada.html) — Wedding officiants in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Ontario: a marriage must be performed by an authorized officiant under the Marriage Act. Registered officiants: persons recognized by their religious body, or by a First Nation, Métis or Inuit organization or community, and registered. Civil officiants: municipal clerks or their delegates, judges, associate judges, justices of the peace, and MPPs who have given written notice. Fees: no set fee under the Act for registered religious officiants; a required $75 fee for marriages by an Ontario judge or justice of the peace (remitted to the Minister of Finance); municipalities may charge for civil ceremonies. Licence and witnesses: the couple, witnesses and officiant sign the licence or banns immediately after the ceremony. Other provinces: Quebec civil marriage $324 plus taxes at a courthouse or city hall, $431 plus taxes elsewhere (2026); Manitoba marriage commissioner $50 plus expenses. Toronto: civic centre wedding chambers $136.85 per 30 minutes including HST; park ceremonies $260.07 an hour including taxes. Example amounts are made up.
- [Wedding insurance](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/wedding-insurance-canada-cancellation-liability.html) — Wedding insurance in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Two parts: cancellation or postponement cover (reimburses non-refundable deposits and contracted costs if the wedding is cancelled or cut short for a listed reason) and special event liability cover (third-party bodily injury or property damage claims, often with a host liquor liability endorsement). Example policy wording (P.A.L. Weddinguard, updated 1 Jun 2024): covered causes include death, injury, illness, quarantine, jury duty or involuntary unemployment (must qualify for EI) of the couple or listed immediate family; overseas job posting; venue unable to host after damage, disease outbreak or insolvency; bridal attire lost or damaged within five working days; transport no-show; extreme weather on the day if bound 15+ days before. Exclusions include disinclination to marry, damage to tents or marquees, pregnancy or childbirth, prior terminal diagnosis, communicable disease leading to quarantine or advisories. $100 deductible per loss per section. Other sections: honeymoon cancellation, vendor financial failure, live entertainer no-show, photographer no-show, attire, gifts, rings, cake and flowers, stationery, rented property. Requirements: Ontario special occasion permit rules do not require liability insurance but venues may; Toronto requires $2 million liability naming the City for commercial photography in parks; Toronto picnic permit insurance $33.48 (1-25 people) or $65.88 (26-100). Example amounts are made up.
- [Planner vs day-of coordinator](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/wedding-planner-vs-day-of-coordinator-cost.html) — Wedding planner vs day-of coordinator in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Levels: full planning (budget, vendor search, contracts, design, logistics, day-of), partial planning (help with selected vendors plus day-of), day-of or month-of coordination (takes over in the final weeks, runs the timeline, rehearsal and day). Pricing models: flat package fee, percentage of the wedding budget, or hourly; ask which and what triggers extra charges. - [Wedding dress costs](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/wedding-dress-cost-canada-alterations-resale.html) — Wedding dress costs in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Budget items: dress, alterations, taxes (Ontario HST 13%, CRA), accessories, cleaning or preservation. Ontario Consumer Protection Act: an ordered product must be delivered within 30 days of the promised delivery date or you can ask for a refund, but keeping a late item loses that right; misrepresentation allows withdrawal within 1 year; cooling-off periods do not apply to ordinary retail orders. Importing by mail: under the Postal Imports Remission Order, items worth CAN$20 or less are free of duty and tax; above CAN$20, duty, GST/HST and any PST apply on the full value (CBSA). Textile labelling: new consumer textile articles must show fibre content and dealer identity; care information is not mandatory but must not be misleading if given; articles clearly identified as second-hand do not require labelling (Competition Bureau). Resale: a dress is personal-use property; CRA says losses on personal-use property generally are not deductible. Example amounts are made up.
- [Suit or tux: rent or buy](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/wedding-suit-tux-rent-vs-buy-canada.html) — Wedding suit or tux, rent vs buy, Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Rentals: ask what the price includes (jacket, trousers, shirt, tie, vest, shoes, cufflinks), fitting and measurement deadlines, pickup and return dates, late and damage fees, and group or groom-free offers. Buying: tailoring extra; a dark suit can be worn again; formal tuxedos are worn less often. Taxes: Ontario HST 13% (CRA). - [Wedding bands](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/wedding-bands-metals-prices-canada.html) — Wedding bands in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026 (Competition Bureau Guide to the Precious Metals Marking Act). Quality marks are optional, but if applied they must be truthful, in the prescribed form and accompanied by a registered or applied-for Canadian trademark (UK hallmarks and foreign government marks are exceptions). Gold: karat marks allowed for 9K or higher; 10K, 14K and 18K may be marked .417, .583, .750 (also 417, 583, 750). Tolerance for gold: 3 parts per 1,000 without solder (7 with solder). Silver: sterling or .925 needs at least 925 parts per 1,000. Platinum: at least 95% platinum (or with iridium or ruthenium); palladium: 95%; no legal tolerance. Gold plated or G.E.P.: plated with at least 10K gold; plating thickness may be marked in whole micrometres if at least 1 micrometre. A dealer cannot mark a plated article guaranteeing plating durability for a period. Tax: jewellery is listed personal property; CRA uses a $1,000 minimum for proceeds and cost. Example amounts are made up.
- [Name change after marriage](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/name-change-after-marriage-canada.html) — Name change after marriage, Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Ontario: you can assume your spouse's last name on your health card, driver's licence and Ontario Photo Card at no cost; it does not change your Ontario birth registration. Visit ServiceOntario with your marriage certificate (not the Record of Solemnization; you must apply, it is not automatic), photo health card and driver's licence or Photo Card. You must record the full last name as on the certificate, including a hyphenated name; using only part of a hyphenated name needs a legal name change. Updated documents arrive by mail in 6 to 8 weeks. The Election to Change Surname service is discontinued. Marriage certificate: $15 regular online, $45 premium (O. Reg. 511/01 fee $15). SIN: Service Canada says you are required by law to update your record when you change your legal name; a marriage certificate supports a family name after marriage, except for Quebec residents married after 1 Apr 1981; no fee. Passport (IRCC): a name change needs a new passport application, not a renewal; adult fees from 31 Mar 2026: 10-year $163.50, 5-year $122.50. Example amounts are made up.
- [Marriage contracts (prenups)](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/marriage-contract-prenup-ontario-cost.html) — Marriage contracts in Ontario, as of 1 Oct 2026 (Family Law Act). s.52(1): two persons who are married or intend to marry may agree on rights and obligations under the marriage, on separation, annulment, dissolution or death, including ownership or division of property, support, the right to direct education and moral training of children (but not decision-making responsibility or parenting time), and any other matter. s.52(2): a provision limiting a spouse's rights to the matrimonial home under Part II is unenforceable. s.53(2): a cohabitation agreement becomes a marriage contract if the parties marry. s.55(1): domestic contracts are unenforceable unless in writing, signed by the parties and witnessed. s.56(1) and (1.1): a court may disregard provisions on children if in the child's best interests, or child support provisions that are unreasonable under the child support guidelines. s.56(4): a court may set aside a contract or provision if a party failed to disclose significant assets, debts or other liabilities, did not understand its nature or consequences, or otherwise under contract law. s.5(1): on separation, the spouse with the lesser net family property is entitled to half the difference; s.4(2) excludes some property, including gifts or inheritances from third persons after marriage (other than a matrimonial home) and property excluded by a domestic contract. Law Society Referral Service: free consultation of up to 30 minutes. Example amounts are made up.
- [Merging finances](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/merging-finances-after-wedding-canada.html) — Merging finances after marriage in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. FCAC lists three ways couples share finances: pool everything in a shared account; hybrid (personal accounts plus a joint account for shared expenses); separate finances with shared costs split. Decide transfer frequency, contribution split (50/50 or by income) and what happens if income drops. Joint accounts (FCAC): each holder is responsible for transactions by the other, including overdraft debts; ask what happens on death, as in some provinces the survivor may not be able to access funds. Credit cards (FCAC): co-applicants are equally responsible for the balance; authorized users are not responsible and do not build credit history; the primary cardholder pays for authorized users' purchases. Co-signing a loan makes you equally responsible. CDIC: insures eligible deposits up to $100,000 per category per member institution, with joint deposits a separate category. CRA TFSA: in provinces that recognize TFSA beneficiary designations, a survivor can be named successor holder and the TFSA continues tax-free. Ontario Family Law Act: net family property deducts debts and the net value of property owned on the marriage date (other than a matrimonial home). Example amounts are made up.
- [Paying for a wedding without debt](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/pay-for-wedding-without-debt-canada.html) — Paying for a wedding without debt, Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Cash budget = savings already set aside + monthly saving x months until final payments + confirmed family gifts. Match the saving plan to vendor deposit and balance dates. Borrowing (FCAC): personal loans commonly $100 to $50,000 over 6 to 60 months; by law lenders may not charge more than 35% a year including fees and interest; longer terms cost more in total. Credit cards (FCAC): federally regulated issuers must give a minimum 21-day interest-free grace period on purchases, not on cash advances; missing a payment can end a promotional rate; issuers must disclose the end date, covered transactions, fees and the standard rate after an introductory rate. Balance transfers (FCAC): usually a fee as a percentage of the amount, promotional rates usually last 6 to 18 months. Merchants may add credit card surcharges up to 2.4% except in Quebec. Example amounts are made up.
- [Card points on wedding spending](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/credit-card-points-wedding-spending-canada.html) — Credit card points on wedding spending, Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Surcharges (FCAC): merchants may add a surcharge to credit card transactions except in Quebec, capped at 2.4%, not higher than their actual cost of acceptance, not in addition to a service or convenience fee; they must disclose it before the transaction, and you must be able to cancel without penalty and pay another way such as debit or cash. Under the Code of Conduct for the Payment Card Industry, merchants may offer discounts for different payment methods. Grace period (FCAC): federally regulated issuers must give at least 21 days interest-free on purchases if the balance is paid in full; none on cash advances. Introductory rates: issuers must disclose end date, covered transactions, fees and the standard rate after. Rewards (FCAC): carrying a balance, interest and fees can outweigh rewards. Example amounts are made up.

- [Tipping wedding vendors](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/tipping-wedding-vendors-canada.html) — Tipping wedding vendors in Canada, as of 1 Oct 2026. Service charges vs tips: under CRA rules a mandatory service charge is part of the taxable price (13% HST in Ontario), while a voluntary tip is not taxed. Ontario Employment Standards Act: tips or other gratuities include gratuity or service charges imposed by banquet halls or other establishments where a reasonable person would believe the payment would be kept by or shared among employees; employers generally cannot withhold, deduct from or make employees return tips, except for tip pools; employers can keep tips they receive themselves; an employer can share in a tip pool only if a sole proprietor, partner, director or shareholder who regularly performs to a substantial degree the same work; employers may exclude part of a credit card processing fee from tips (the greater of the card company's percentage or 1.5% of the tip), but not debit or other processing fees. Tips must be paid by cash, cheque or direct deposit to an account the employee chooses (since 21 Jun 2024). Example amounts are made up.

- [Marriage and your will](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/marriage-will-ontario-2022-change.html) — Marriage and wills in Ontario, as of 1 Oct 2026 (Succession Law Reform Act). Since 1 Jan 2022, s.15(a) (revocation by marriage) and s.16 are repealed, so marriage no longer revokes a will; a will is revoked only by a later will, a written revocation made like a will, or destruction with intent. s.17(2): divorce or nullity revokes gifts to, and appointments of, the former spouse unless the will shows a contrary intention. s.17(3)-(4): the same applies if spouses are separated at death: living apart for three years before death due to breakdown, a valid separation agreement, a court order or a family arbitration award, and living apart at death. Intestacy: s.44 spouse and no issue takes everything; s.45 spouse and issue: spouse takes the preferential share, $350,000 for deaths on or after 1 Mar 2021 (O. Reg. 54/95); s.46 spouse takes half the residue with one child, one-third with two or more. s.43.1: intestacy entitlements do not apply to separated spouses. 'Spouse' for intestacy means married (Family Law Act s.1), not common-law. Family Law Act s.6: a surviving spouse elects to take under the will or an equalization entitlement, filed within six months of death. O. Reg. 54/95 s.2: TFSAs are prescribed plans for beneficiary designations. Example amounts are made up.

Black Friday is Friday 27 Nov 2026, Cyber Monday is Monday 30 Nov 2026, Boxing Day is Saturday 26 Dec 2026. Competition Bureau: a regular price used to claim a saving must meet the volume test (more than 50% of sales at that price or higher within a reasonable period, usually within a year, before or after the promotion) or the time test (offered in good faith at that price or higher for a substantial period, usually within a year, immediately before or after). Fake urgency cues (resetting countdown timers, false low-stock claims), bait and switch, and drip pricing (mandatory non-government fees left out of the advertised price) can be misleading under the Competition Act. Formula: watts / 1,000 x hours x price per kWh. Ontario Energy Board prices set for 1 Nov 2025 and still shown as current (electricity price only, before delivery, regulatory charges, HST and the Ontario Electricity Rebate): TOU off-peak 9.8, mid-peak 15.7, on-peak 20.3 cents/kWh; ULO overnight 3.9, weekend off-peak 9.8, mid-peak 15.7, on-peak 39.1 cents/kWh; Tiered 12.0 and 14.2 cents/kWh, winter residential threshold 1,000 kWh/month (1 Nov to 30 Apr). Canadian Transportation Agency (page modified 26 Feb 2026): compensation for delays within the airline's control and not required for safety, when notified 14 days or less before departure and arriving 3 or more hours late, claimed in writing within 1 year: large airlines $400 (3 to under 6 hours), $700 (6 to under 9), $1,000 (9 or more); small airlines $125, $250, $500. Large Canadian airlines: Air Canada (including Jazz and Rouge), WestJet, Sunwing, Air Transat, Porter and Flair. Weather delays are outside the airline's control (rebooking, no compensation). Ontario winter driving: keep the tank at least half full; check Ontario 511. Intercity buses often win on price for solo travellers on short and medium routes. Example costs are made up.
- [Year-end money moves before Dec 31](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/year-end-money-moves-canada-before-december-31.html) — Year-end money moves in Canada for 2026, as of 7 Oct 2026. Donations: claim up to 75% of net income; unused gifts can be carried forward 5 years (CRA). Tax-loss selling: CRA's T5008 guide uses the settlement date; TSX trades settle T+1; TSX 2026 holidays Dec 24 (1 p.m. close), Dec 25 and Mon Dec 28 (in lieu of Boxing Day); a trade on Thu Dec 31, 2026 settles Mon Jan 4, 2027, so Wed Dec 30 is the last regular trade date that settles in 2026 (confirm your broker's cut-off). Superficial loss: you or an affiliated person buys identical property from 30 days before to 30 days after the sale and still holds it 30 days after. FHSA: $8,000 annual participation room (contributions and transfers combined, per calendar year), $40,000 lifetime; deduction counts contributions made by Dec 31. RESP CESG: 20% up to $500 a year per child ($1,000 with unused room), lifetime $7,200. RDSP contribution, grant and bond deadline: Dec 31. TFSA: withdrawals come back as room on Jan 1 of the following year. Medical expenses: any 12-month period ending in the tax year; threshold is the lesser of 3% of net income or a fixed amount ($2,834 for 2025). Dec 31 of the year you turn 71 is the last day to contribute to your own RRSP. Worked example inputs are made up.

Ontario Ticket Sales Act, 2017 (ontario.ca, updated June 4, 2026): it is illegal to resell tickets, or facilitate resale, for more than the original total price paid to the primary seller; a resale buyer pays no more than the original total price plus applicable taxes and the resale platform's standard fees; resale listings must show the original total price, itemized fees and taxes, and total resale price; buyers must get proof of validity from the primary seller or a written money-back guarantee; primary sellers must show the total price in Canadian dollars with itemized fees; ticket bots are banned. Competition Bureau: drip pricing (advertising a price that cannot be attained because of mandatory fixed non-government fees) is false or misleading. - [CPP at 60, 65 or 70? Plus the OAS clawback](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/cpp-at-60-65-or-70-oas-clawback-canada.html) — CPP and OAS timing in Canada, as of 7 Oct 2026. CPP retirement pension: start between 60 and 70; payments fall 0.6% a month before 65 (7.2% a year, up to 36% at 60) and rise 0.7% a month after 65 (8.4% a year, up to 42% at 70); no benefit to waiting past 70. Maximum CPP at 65 (January 2026) $1,507.65 a month; average at 65 (July 2026) $858.34 a month. OAS pension: start between 65 and 70; deferral adds 0.6% a month, up to 36% at 70; maximum Oct-Dec 2026: $762.50 a month at 65-74, $838.75 at 75+ (10% increase at 75 since July 2022); deferred to 70: $1,037.00. If you do not receive OAS you cannot get the GIS; GIS does not increase with deferral. OAS recovery tax: 15% of net world income above the threshold; $93,454 for 2025 income (July 2026 to June 2027), $95,323 for 2026 income (July 2027 to June 2028); full OAS repaid at 2025 income of $152,062 (65-74) or $157,923 (75+). Simple break-even with a made-up $1,000 at 65 (ignoring indexing, tax and returns): 60 vs 65 about age 74; 65 vs 70 about age 82. Worked example inputs are made up.
